newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends mostly weak on technicals, CBOT.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends mostly weak on technicals, CBOT.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled mostly lower as losses from technically oriented selling were compounded by spillover weakness from a late sag in CBOT soybeans and wheat, traders said.
KCBT wheat was under pressure throughout the session from technically related speculative selling after the July contract failed to pierce resistance at $4.56 per bushel.

KCBT wheat managed to climb off its lows toward the midsession on strength from a rally in soybeans, but wheat values subsequently turned weaker as CBOT wheat and soybeans sagged in a late-session sell-off.
U.S. wheat markets also drew pressure from forecasts for rain next week in parched areas of Britain and France.
Traders said KCBT wheat appeared to shrug off a survey by Oklahoma State University that estimated nearly 41 percent of Oklahoma's wheat crop would be lost because of damage from a mid-April freeze.
"The market just seems to be ho-hum about damage to the Oklahoma crop," a trader said, adding that KCBT wheat also seemed to brush off talk of cold temperatures this weekend in the U.S. Midwest.
KCBT wheat settled steady to five cents per bushel lower, with May unchanged at $4.57. New crop July lost 4-1/4 cents to close at $4.50.

FIMAT Futures was a featured player, selling 1.8 million July and one million September bushels, but also buying one million July. Prudential Securities sold 1.3 million September and one million December bushels, traders said.
